insert: * DOCTRINE PATCH: the NEXUS Tank (ScavNEXUStrack + ScavNEXUSlink) captures your
* units and buildings outright, has 225 HP and 14 kinetic armour — 3.5x a Viper
* body — and cost the scavs only 29 power to field. With nothing but starting
* MGs there is no answer to it, so it is now held back until NEXUS_TANK_AFTER.
* Before that the same factory slot builds an ordinary scav tank instead.
const NEXUS_TANK_AFTER = 20 * 60 * 1000;   // ms of game time — 20 minutes
Stock uuscav2 allows 16 scavenger factories and 8 VTOL factories, each of
which builds whenever idle on a 1-second timer. Measured on a headless
4-AI run that compounds into 138 scav units by 7 minutes and 240 by 8,
and every AI was dead by 9:40 with an army of 0-3 tanks. The same map
without this mod: AIs reached 9-13 tanks, held 4-6 derricks each and were
all still alive at 19 minutes against 167 scavengers.
So the scavengers were not "formidable", they were terminal. These caps
keep the early pressure — the factory ceiling is not reached for several
minutes — while stopping the late exponential.  */
Stock uuscav2 rolls a random body and a random weapon from the FULL arsenal
from the first second of the game, so AT rockets, flamers and cannon
half-tracks can show up before a player has a second structure standing, and
VTOLs arrive at six minutes. The scavengers now climb a ladder instead:
0:00-2:00   holding back. Economy only -- trucks, sensors, derricks. No
combat units, and no offensive orders at all.
2:00-3:30   still economy, but the hold on attacking is lifted so anything
already fielded (and the map's pre-placed scavengers) reacts.
6:00-10:00  medium: adds cannons and basic rockets on heavier bodies.
10:00+      heavy: AT rockets, flamers, 3x-cannon heavy tanks.
The NEXUS capture tank stays on its own 20-minute timer above.  */
const SCAV_T_HOLD   = 120e3;   // no offensive orders before this
const SCAV_T_MEDIUM = 360e3;   // cannons and basic rockets
const SCAV_T_HEAVY  = 600e3;   // AT rockets, flamers, heavy tanks
const SCAV_T_AIR    = 900e3;   // VTOL factories and helicopters (15 min)
const SCAV_T_AIR2   = 1200e3;  // heavy napalm bombs (20 min)
const SCAV_T_BOMBER = 600e3;   // suicide bomb trucks (10 min)
/* The blast a scavenger bomb truck leaves behind.
There is no data field that attaches an explosion to a droid -- the scavenger
power generator's famous detonation is engine-side, keyed off the structure
TYPE, and cannot be borrowed. What the scripting API does give us is
fireWeaponAtLoc(weapon, x, y, player), the same call the campaign uses to
bring down the LasSat: it plays the weapon's real explosion and applies its
real damage at a point, in tile coordinates.
Bomb2-VTOL-HvHE is the one that behaves like a bomb: 500 on the point of
impact and 300 splash out to 256 (two tiles). The incendiary bombs look the
part but have radius 0 -- they would have gone off with no blast at all. */
/* A vehicle with three turrets engages at ONE distance, so mixing a 2304-range
mortar with a 384-range flamer means two of the three barrels are decoration.
There is no scripting call to force an engagement range, so instead every
turret on a multi-slot vehicle is drawn from the SAME range band -- then
whatever distance it fights at, all three weapons reach.
Bands are keyed off longRange: flamer 384, the general-purpose guns 960,
/* Pick a band that this phase can actually field, then three turrets from it. */
/* Its gun reaches 224 -- shorter than the 256 blast it carries -- so it has
to drive into the kill zone before it can shoot at all. With BaBaMG (960)
it simply parked at machinegun range and never detonated on anything. */
/* Bomb trucks come in three grades rather than one. A suicide truck only pays
off if it REACHES something, and the stock ice van (136hp) died on the run-in
now that its gun reaches only 40. ScavBomberBody is a reinforced van built by
the mod for this one job (340hp, armour 8) so buffing it does not also buff
every technical sharing the ice van; the later grades trade a little of that
toughness for the heavier chassis the scavengers earn over the game. */
// 3:30 -- the improvised one: a van with a bomb in the back
// 6:00 -- purpose-built, and a bus packed with scrap
/* Every bomber name, so eventDestroyed knows what detonates. */
for (var j = 0; j < SCAV_BOMBERS[i].length; ++j) { seen[SCAV_BOMBERS[i][j].name] = true; }
/* Emplacements the scavengers picket their own oil and outposts with, phased
the same way their vehicles are. Gun towers are dirt cheap (75 build points)
so the opening picket costs them almost nothing; the rocket pits are held
back until they have earned the right to field AT. */
// Bunkers from the second phase, and listed twice from the third: they are
// the toughest thing the scavengers can plant (600hp, BUNKER class, so
// artillery does only 45% to them) and a dug-in derrick should mostly be
/* How many emplacements may stand within PICKET_RADIUS of one derrick or
outpost. Two is a picket; more is the carpet we removed earlier. */
/* Raised from 2. Two emplacements is a token; four is a position worth
attacking around, which is what "fortify the derricks" has to mean. */
// 3:30 — the junkyard tier: thin, cheap, slow to assemble
// 6:00 — the light "-Ultimate" shells arrive: a little tougher and roughly
// four times quicker to build, plus the rocket-buggy chassis
// 10:00 — the heavy shells, and the wheeled NEXUS body (180hp, armour 10)
/* ...and a ceiling on emplacements. Capping only the units displaced the
problem rather than fixing it: the trucks, no longer feeding factories,
poured everything into the loop's fallback branch instead and put up 270
mortar pits and cannon towers by 12 minutes. */
/* Raised from 24 to carry the deeper pickets. Note the counter below now
counts EVERY defence the scavengers own -- it used to count only mortar
pits and cannon towers, so bunkers, gun towers, rocket pits and flame
towers were all invisible to this ceiling and effectively unlimited. */
/* Total fielded combat units, ramped so the early rush is undiminished and the
plateau lands a little above vanilla ultimate scavengers rather than 3x it. */
/* How much of the unit ceiling the scavengers give to infantry. */
/* ...and the most of the unit ceiling that may be helicopters. VTOLs are
counted by enumDroid(me, DROID_WEAPON) exactly like tanks, so without a
separate ceiling the air arm just outbid the ground arm for the same slots:
the VTOL factories need only 150 power to run where the ground factories
need 250. Capping the air share puts the land army back. */
// Hard floor first: no scavenger air before SCAV_T_AIR, whatever the tech
// level or base setting says. Stock allowed VTOL factories from 6:00 (and
// immediately at tech level 2+), which is well before a player has AA.
/* factory id -> how many more infantry this factory still owes. Scavengers
turn out squads, not individuals: one roll books THREE bodies and the
factory delivers them back to back before it considers anything else. */
/* Anything the scavengers own that is supposed to go off when it dies.
Bomb trucks are the obvious case; their power generators are the other, and
both want the same treatment, so they share one handler. */
if (obj.type === DROID && SCAV_BOMBER_NAMES[obj.name] === true) blast = true
else if (obj.type === STRUCTURE && obj.stattype === POWER_GEN) blast = true
try { fireWeaponAtLoc(SCAV_BLAST, obj.x, obj.y, me) } catch (e) { }
/* rules/setup/scavengers.js hands the scavenger player a fixed component list.
Three things we now want are missing from it, so they are enabled once here:
the Ultimate INFANTRY shell (the vehicle Ultimates are already on the list,
the infantry one is not), and the two incendiary bombs for the choppers.
The scavenger walls are likewise not in their enabled-structure list. */
for (var c = 0; c < COMPONENTS.length; ++c) makeComponentAvailable(COMPONENTS[c], me)
for (var t = 0; t < STRUCTS.length; ++t) enableStructure(STRUCTS[t], me)
// Picket our OWN derricks and outposts first. Stock uuscav2 only
// ever emplaced next to ENEMY oil (protectCloseDerrick) -- its own
// wells stood bare all game. Runs from the first minute; the type
if (!pos) { return } // no legal site near this truck this tick
if (!nx) { nx={x:x+1,y:y} } // off the flow field: any direction will do
// Tiers accumulate rather than replace: everything ever unlocked stays
// in the pool, with the newest tier entered twice so it dominates the
// roll. High-tier scavs keep fielding trikes and MG infantry alongside
// the heavy kit instead of abruptly abandoning them.
// Infantry come in PAIRS: the roll below builds the first and flags
// the factory, and its next idle tick builds the twin before
// Infantry are the BULK of the horde, not the whole of it. An absolute
// floor was a mistake: it read 8+6/min capped at 70 while the total
// unit ceiling is 60, so it could never be satisfied and the ground
// factories built infantry and nothing else -- measured at zero tanks
// and zero bomb trucks across a 55-minute game. It is a SHARE of the
// ceiling now, and even under that share one tick in three still goes
// to vehicles, so armour always keeps trickling out.
// Infantry come FIRST and never stop. Scavengers are people before they
// are vehicles: below the running floor below, a factory builds nothing
// else -- not trucks, not sensors -- and the floor climbs all game, so
// the horde keeps growing rather than plateauing early.
// Only the WHEELED arsenal stays phase-gated; in phase 0 anything that
// is not infantry becomes another truck, funding the early expansion.
// all three turrets from one range band -- see SCAV_BANDS
// too early for the capture unit — build a normal tank instead
if (airborne>=airCap) return   // the air arm has had its share
// Holding back: for the opening SCAV_T_HOLD the scavengers do not go
// looking for anyone. They still defend themselves (the engine handles
// that) and still collect oil drums above.
